summary: This component renders a blog tag page that displays all articles with a specific tag. It first extracts the tag slug from the URL, looks up the original tag name from blog post metadata, filters posts that match that tag, and displays them in a grid along with RSS feed links. If no tag is specified or no posts exist for that tag, it shows an appropriate error message.

explanations.17: This type definition says a Tag can be either a simple string like 'javascript' or an object with a label property, allowing for more complex tag structures in the front matter.
explanations.24: The useSourceLocaleUrls hook returns information about whether we're on the default language version of the site and URLs/labels for the original language, used later for showing a source language feed link.
explanations.28: The comment is explaining that the URL pattern needs to include baseUrl because on non-default locales like French, the actual pathname includes the locale prefix (e.g., /fr/blog/tags/slug instead of /blog/tags/slug).
explanations.32: This removes any trailing slash from the base URL so the pattern matching works correctly—baseUrl might be '/' or '/my-site/' but we need a consistent format.
explanations.33: matchPath tries to parse the current URL against the pattern we defined, extracting the tag slug if it matches; if it doesn't match, match will be null.
explanations.37: We safely extract the slug parameter from the match result—this could be undefined if the URL didn't match our pattern.
explanations.58: This helper function extracts the actual tag key/name from a Tag, handling both the simple string case and the object case where the key is nested under the label property.
explanations.64: We convert the tag through getTagKey to get its string value, then create a slug from it (lowercase, remove special chars, etc.) to compare it with the URL slug.
explanations.75: tagLabel is a function that takes the tag key and returns its display name with any translations applied—so 'ai' might become 'Artificial Intelligence (AI)'.
explanations.82: We sort posts by date in descending order—the `.getTime()` on dates and subtracting b from a puts most recent posts first.
explanations.142: If we're not on the default locale (meaning we're viewing a translated version), we add a second RSS link pointing back to the source language's full blog feed.
